cursor.note: PROVED. The hollow verb reverts a file and reads the teeth — and the defect this voyage found was not that it failed, it was that it SUCCEEDED WRONGLY. Two causes, and only the second one mattered. (1) git exports GIT_INDEX_FILE=.git/index — a RELATIVE path — plus GIT_PREFIX= into every hook, and the pre-commit hook runs the reseal door, which runs proofs as subprocesses that inherit it; scratch_worktree died loudly under that env in 0.12s, which is the honest failure and was fixed first. (2) hollow._restore, a `git -C <worktree> checkout -- <rel>`, resolved against the CALLER's index instead of the worktree's, did nothing, said nothing, and returned nothing to look at. So file N stayed reverted while file N+1 was measured, N+1's teeth redded for a reason that had nothing to do with N+1, that red read as 'a declared tooth checks this file', and A FILE THAT REALLY WAS HOLLOW WAS REPORTED ok — a hollow read as green, manufactured inside the catcher whose whole job is catching one (Law 8: a false green gets leaned on by a peer; that is why it is worse than a red). `git -C <root>` is not a defence anywhere, because GIT_DIR and its siblings outrank it everywhere. THE FIX IS TWO THINGS, and the second is the one that generalises: _git_env became public git_env() and every git call in the tester that means 'the repository I am pointing at' now takes it (3 in scratch.py, 4 in hollow.py, the fixtures in test_hollow.py); and _restore RAISES HollowUnmeasurable when the checkout fails, because the next thing that stops a checkout will not be an env var and the verb must not go on measuring past it (Law 3: a measurement that could not be taken may not travel home through the same return as a clean one). A 13th tooth pins that raise, and it is deliberately not coupled to the env var that revealed it — it makes the checkout fail by pointing at a directory that is no repository. Mutation-verified: stub the guard to `if False:` and it fails; restore it and it passes. THE LINE THAT IS NOT OVER-APPLIED, recorded in the docstring because it is easy to get wrong: reseal.staged_files must NOT scrub. Under `git commit -a` git writes a TEMPORARY index and points GIT_INDEX_FILE at it, so the hook's staged set lives there and nowhere else; scrubbing would read the pre-`-a` index and reseal the wrong proofs. A call meaning 'the repository I am pointing at' scrubs; a call meaning 'the index my caller is committing' must not. MEASURED: test_hollow.py under GIT_INDEX_FILE=.git/index GIT_PREFIX= went from 4 failed to 12 passed in 311.64s, and seals 13 teeth_green / 0 teeth_red. Live fire `cairn test --seal --hollow 9579a6f9cec6` at HEAD 3159682: 8 measured · 0 hollow · 2 skipped, exit 0, 'SEALED — hollow evidence landed on 3 of 3 standing validation(s)', wall clock 2m7s against the ticket's 5-minute WRONG INTENT threshold — so the shared-worktree redesign that clause calls for is not owed. All three seals carry exactly the eight ratified fields and evidence.hollow['9579a6f9cec6'] over 8 files. OWED, MEASURED, AND DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED HERE: 12 proof files and 11 non-proof modules shell `git -C <root>` and only 2 scrub — test_inspector.py, test_history_integrity.py and test_forwarding_derivation.py bare-inherit, test_ruling.py inherits os.environ straight into git. They are out of this voyage's bounds for a structural reason, not a tired one: git_env lives in cairn.devices.tester.scratch, so build_inspector's and ruling's proofs cannot import it without a cross-device import (ruled: only db_domain). Its right home is a tool, and picking that rung is design work, not a patch.

window.note: THE SEAL VOCABULARY'S AXIS IS WHETHER THE SEAL WAS ASKED FOR, which is why three of its four words are measurements and only `open` is the absence of one — and why `sealed -> open` is the single transition that retires a measurement rather than recording a newer one. On 2026-09-08 a blanket re-seal made that transition 44 times and nothing refused it; it was caught by diffing one file by hand. Two acts close it, because a guard alone would have punished a caller who meant the right thing: persist_validation now refuses sealed|indeterminate|breached -> open unless the caller states `unsealing_because`, which then rides permanently inside the record's evidence (the escape is on the record, never ambient) and fires BEFORE the announce and the write, so a refused write leaves the standing record untouched; and `cairn test --seal` asks each proof what isolation its standing seal was taken at and reproduces THAT, so the ordinary re-seal never meets the guard at all. sealed->breached, sealed->indeterminate and open->sealed all pass unrefused: a guard blocking a newer RED would be Law 7 inverted at the door Law 7 exists for. THE PER-PROOF READ IS VISIBLE AS A DISTRIBUTION rather than a word: the tester's own eight re-sealed at netns=4 none=4, the twelve out-of-component proofs fingerprinting a file this voyage changed at netns=11 none=1, and every one of the nineteen carrying a seal at HEAD reproduced it with zero guard refusals — including the three the blanket sweep had reddened and build_inspector's test_inspector, which carries seal:open because it times out at 120s inside a netns. One typed flag would have had to be wrong for one of those groups. A SECOND DEFECT IN THE SAME FUNCTION was fixed here under ruling 2026-09-09-a-bug-the-voyage-uncovers-is-fixed-by-that-voyage: the --seal summary printed `total - n_red` persisted while its own next clause said 'a red seals its red' (49 proofs, 6 red, printed 43, 49 on disk) — a Law 7 lie misreporting the very count this ticket is about. Five teeth, green twice, both mutations bite. And two deviations from the chart are in the verdict rather than smoothed over: hypothesis 1's falsifier fixed a corpus SNAPSHOT where it meant an invariant, and the probe's `enough` holds a floor on the sealed COUNT where the spec named a RATIO — a ratio falls when someone honestly adds an unsealed proof, so it would poke the owner about the system working.

window.note: `cairn test --hollow <ticket>` built across three pieces: scratch.scratch_worktree (a worktree deregistered at exit, because the .git/worktrees half of the leak is the invisible one), hollow.py + the verb, and validation_store.record_hollow landing the reading as evidence.hollow[ticket] on the standing seal through the store's one door. 10 teeth green 4 runs back to back, 0 worktree registrations left. FOUR states not two: covered, hollow, `unreadable` (the proof died on import, which reds every tooth and would otherwise read as perfect coverage) and `unwritten` (the revert changed nothing, a finding against the chart's writes_to). A run in which every file was skipped is a RED. FIXED IN FLIGHT under ruling 2026-09-09-a-bug-the-voyage-uncovers-is-fixed-by-that-voyage: same-size same-second rewrites reused stale __pycache__, so the verb read a tree that did not exist and credited the wrong file for a red — 3 wrong answers in 14 runs, now purged before every run and held by a tooth that FORCES the collision rather than waiting for it.
